results.claim: Last-move compression: if H is k-uniform and its classical Maker-Breaker duration τ(H)=t is finite, then θ(H)≤max{k,t−1}. More precisely, θ(H)=k when t=k, while θ(H)≤t−1 when t>k.
results.proof_sketch: Every win requires k simultaneous Maker tokens, so t≥k and θ(H)≥k. Fix a classical strategy S winning within t Maker moves. In the limited-token game, represent every Breaker pass or relocation by a virtual classical move: retain all earlier virtual blue claims and add a legal new virtual blue claim, using the actual destination when possible and otherwise a free filler. The actual blue set remains contained in the virtual one, so every vertex prescribed by S is actually free. Maker follows S with fresh tokens for her first t−1 moves. An earlier win finishes the game. Otherwise, on move t, S prescribes a vertex x completing a k-edge e. The other k−1 vertices of e are among Maker's t−1 current tokens. If t>k, at least (t−1)−(k−1)=t−k≥1 token lies outside e; moving it to x completes e without vacating e. Thus θ(H)≤t−1. If t=k, the same simulation uses k fresh tokens, while fewer than k tokens cannot fill a k-edge, so θ(H)=k.

results.claim: Uniform strict half-bound: every finite-theta k-uniform hypergraph H on n vertices satisfies θ(H)≤max{k,⌊(n−1)/2⌋}. In particular, if n≥2k+1 then θ(H)≤⌈n/2⌉−1.
results.proof_sketch: Finite θ(H) implies τ(H)<∞ by monotonicity in Maker's token supply. The classical duration bound gives τ(H)≤⌈n/2⌉; Breaker passes or relocations can again be replaced by virtual fresh claims and cannot make Maker's task harder. Applying last-move compression yields θ(H)≤max{k,τ(H)−1}≤max{k,⌈n/2⌉−1}=max{k,⌊(n−1)/2⌋}. When n≥2k+1, one has ⌈n/2⌉>k, so the maximum is exactly ⌈n/2⌉−1, strictly below the former half-vertex bound.

results.claim: Exact order obstruction: a finite k-uniform hypergraph can attain θ(H)=⌈n/2⌉ only when n∈{2k−1,2k}; both orders are attainable.
results.proof_sketch: If θ(H)=⌈n/2⌉ and ⌈n/2⌉>k, the strict half-bound gives the contradiction θ(H)≤⌈n/2⌉−1. Since filling a k-edge requires at least k tokens, equality also forces ⌈n/2⌉≥k. Consequently ⌈n/2⌉=k, equivalently n∈{2k−1,2k}. Conversely, on either order let H contain every k-subset as an edge. Fewer than k tokens cannot fill an edge. With k tokens, Maker places a new token on each of her first k turns. Before her kth turn at most 2k−2 vertices have been occupied, so a free vertex remains; after taking it, her k vertices form an edge. Thus θ(H)=k=⌈n/2⌉.

final_writeup:
No fixed k≥4 admits arbitrarily large examples attaining the half-vertex bound. Indeed, the stronger uniform estimate

θ(H) ≤ max{k, ⌊(n−1)/2⌋}

holds for every k-uniform H on n vertices with finite token number. Therefore, for every n≥2k+1,

θ(H) ≤ ⌈n/2⌉−1.

The key observation is that the final move of a bounded classical winning strategy does not require a new token. Let t=τ(H), and fix a classical strategy winning within t Maker moves. Breaker passes or relocations can be represented by a virtual classical history that retains all previous blue claims and adds a legal fresh blue claim each turn. The actual blue set is contained in the virtual one, so every move prescribed by the classical strategy remains actually available.

If t>k, Maker follows this strategy using fresh tokens for the first t−1 moves. On any branch that lasts until move t, the prescribed final vertex x completes a k-edge e. Exactly k−1 vertices of e were previously held, whereas Maker currently has t−1>k−1 tokens. She can therefore move a token situated outside e to x, retaining all of e and winning with only t−1 tokens. If t=k, exactly k tokens suffice. Thus

θ(H)≤max{k,τ(H)−1}.

Finite θ(H) implies finite τ(H), and the classical duration bound τ(H)≤⌈n/2⌉ now proves the displayed estimate, using ⌈n/2⌉−1=⌊(n−1)/2⌋.

This also completely locates possible equality. If θ(H)=⌈n/2⌉ and ⌈n/2⌉>k, the strict bound gives a contradiction. If ⌈n/2⌉<k, equality contradicts the necessary lower bound θ(H)≥k. Hence ⌈n/2⌉=k, equivalently n=2k−1 or n=2k.

Equality occurs at both orders for the complete k-uniform hypergraph. Maker places a fresh token on each of her first k turns. Before her kth turn at most 2k−2 vertices are occupied, so a free vertex remains; her resulting k vertices form an edge. Fewer than k tokens cannot fill an edge, and therefore θ(H)=k=⌈n/2⌉.

Thus equality is confined to two bounded orders for each fixed k, while every n≥2k+1 satisfies the uniform one-step improvement over the half-vertex bound.
